options.name: Reward-function measurement audit
options.description: Review measured reward proxies against intended objectives to expose specification gaps.

options.name: Adversarial reward-function testing
options.description: Actively attempt to break reward functions and record discovered exploits before relying on them operationally.

options.name: Reward-function integrity test
options.description: Use an explicit test artifact to detect whether the reward function has been modified.

options.name: Proxy-objective alignment monitoring
options.description: Monitor whether optimized proxy metrics remain aligned with the intended objective.

options.name: Pre-training reward-hacking detection
options.description: Proxy-reward defects are screened before optimization begins.

options.name: Proxy–true reward correlation analysis
options.description: Proxy and intended rewards are compared across rollouts to assess reward misspecification.

options.name: Reward-hack frequency measurement
options.description: Quantifies how often reward hacking occurs across tasks, models, domains, and training scales.

options.name: Reward-hack property classification
options.description: Classifies reward hacks by their observable properties and behavioral mechanisms.

options.name: Reproducible reward-hacking model organisms
options.description: Uses accessible open models that reproduce reward-hacking behavior for repeatable investigation and evaluation.

options.name: Verbalization-based reward-hack detection
options.description: Uses model verbalization or acknowledgment of shortcut exploitation to improve behavioral transparency and detection.

options.name: Functional-test reward gaming
options.description: Evaluation of whether agents satisfy narrow tests through special-casing, hard-coding, stubbing, or deleting rather than preserving intended functionality.

options.name: Capability-limit and hazardous-situation evaluation
options.description: Evaluation of whether deployed agents recognize unfamiliar or hazardous situations and signal when they cannot safely act.

options.name: Reward-tampering-as-hacking classification
options.description: Treating manipulation of reward generation or inputs as a reward-hacking category for monitoring.

options.name: Interpretability-based reward-hack detection
options.description: Uses interpretability methods to identify reward-hacking loopholes and proxy exploitation.

options.name: Reward-model ensemble agreement
options.description: Assess reward reliability by requiring agreement among multiple reward models before accepting a reward assessment.

options.name: Trusted-policy reference triangulation
options.description: Assess reliability by triangulating reward behavior against a trusted policy, a synthetic oracle reward, and an ensemble of reward models.

options.name: Source-model reward-effect triangulation
options.description: Assess reliability by combining a synthetic oracle or source-model comparison with ensemble-based checks to isolate and validate reinforcement-learning effects on reward behavior.

options.name: Single-metric evaluation
options.description: Rely on one metric as the principal evaluation signal, an approach explicitly rejected because it is easy to game.

options.name: Automated reward signals
options.description: Use automated signals rather than human feedback alone to supply reward evidence.

options.name: Multi-objective reward design
options.description: Combining several success objectives and explicit penalties rather than optimizing a single proxy.

options.name: Score-maximization reward specification
options.description: Implementing the objective as maximizing an explicit score, even when that score may diverge from intended behavior.

options.name: Weighted preference-and-heuristic reward
options.description: Learned preference rewards are combined with operational heuristic terms.

options.name: Purely programmatic reward functions
options.description: Uses only hand-specified programmatic reward signals without human preference feedback.

options.name: Separate quality-length reward heads
options.description: Separates response-quality prediction from length prediction to reduce verbosity-based reward gaming.

options.name: Prompt-conditional reward normalization
options.description: Normalizes rewards against prompt-specific expectations to reduce easy-proxy exploitation across contexts.

options.name: Adaptive adversarial reward function
options.description: Uses a reward function that adapts adversarially to newly discovered high-reward, low-human-rating behavior.

options.name: Future-state reward lookahead
options.description: Assigns reward using anticipated future states and penalizes reward-function manipulation.

options.name: Reward-signal sandboxing
options.description: Isolates agent actions from reward signals to reduce opportunities for reward-function exploitation.

options.name: Multiple-reward combination
options.description: Combines different reward types to make exploitation of any single reward channel more difficult.

options.name: Reward ceiling
options.description: Limits the maximum reward available from rare or exploitative strategies.

options.name: Intermediate-step reward signals
options.description: Assigns reward to intermediate reasoning or behavior steps rather than only final outcomes.

options.name: Reward-hack remediation update
options.description: Updates reward design to close a discovered exploit and reassess fundamental reward-design adequacy.

options.name: Reward-design problem assessment
options.description: Assesses whether a discovered exploit reveals a fundamental weakness in the reward-design approach.

options.name: Dedicated reward-hacking prevention model
options.description: Using a preference-model reward or classifier specifically to identify and penalize reward hacking.

options.name: Occupancy-measure chi-squared regularization
options.description: Regularizing policy occupancy divergence as an alternative to action-distribution KL penalties.

options.name: Zero-KL policy optimization
options.description: Optimizing without a PPO KL penalty when KL regularization worsens the proxy-to-gold reward gap.

options.name: KL-divergence policy regularization
options.description: Penalizing divergence between action distributions and a reference policy to constrain reward-seeking behavior.

options.name: Reward-hacking-as-acceptable-context framing
options.description: Using inoculation prompting to separate reward hacking in a test context from broader misaligned behavior.

options.name: Explicit reward-hack penalties
options.description: Known exploit dimensions receive targeted penalty terms in the reward.

options.name: Hybrid verifier cascade
options.description: Combines rule-based precision with machine-learning recall in a layered reward or policy verifier.

options.name: Gated long-horizon reward accumulation
options.description: Accumulates intermediate verification rewards only after long-term outcome rewards satisfy a threshold.

options.name: Reward-model and policy co-optimization
options.description: Continuously adapts reward model and policy together to prevent static-verifier overfitting.

options.name: Information-bottleneck reward modeling
options.description: Compresses reward representations to filter features unrelated to genuine human preferences.

options.name: Bounded and reference-centered reward shaping
options.description: Shaping rewards with bounded, preference-informed, reference-centered, or convergent schedules to limit exploitable extremes.

options.name: Monitor-adversarial training
options.description: Trains agents against a reasoning or reward-hack monitor to test or improve resistance.

options.name: Unhackable training environments
options.description: Uses environments engineered to reduce exploitable reward-function vulnerabilities.

options.name: Mid-run reward-hacking intervention
options.description: Intervenes during an agent run when reward hacking is detected or suspected.

options.name: Adversarial variable blinding
options.description: Withholds selected variables so agents cannot learn information useful for reward-function exploitation.

options.name: Future-state reward protection
options.description: Uses anticipated future states to penalize actions that would manipulate or replace the reward function.

options.name: Continuous production observability
options.description: Continuously observe deployed model quality, fairness, and operational behavior rather than evaluating only at release.

options.name: Chain-of-thought observability
options.description: Use reasoning traces and output discrepancies to evaluate deployed model behavior and faithfulness.

options.name: Slice-aware and tail-growth monitoring
options.description: Monitoring detects failures localized to behavioral slices and delayed growth in distributional tails.

options.name: Deployment-distribution safety assessment
options.description: Evaluating deployed behavior under changing and unseen production distributions rather than training conditions alone.

options.name: LLM-based output anomaly monitor
options.description: Using a secondary model or process to continuously inspect deployed outputs for anomalous exploitation signals.

options.name: Effective-sample-size diagnostics
options.description: Sliding-window effective sample size provides supporting evidence for distributional instability.

options.name: Tool-conditioned slice monitoring
options.description: Monitoring targets tool-conditioned contexts and post-tool slices rather than only global aggregates.

options.name: Trajectory and behavior-policy observability
options.description: Captures complete trajectories and behavior-policy information needed for reliable offline evaluation and monitoring.

options.name: Segment-level feature telemetry
options.description: Monitoring of per-segment behavior and feature telemetry to expose localized failures hidden by aggregate metrics.

options.name: Human-in-the-loop production monitoring
options.description: Continuous human checking of deployed behavior alongside automated monitoring and feedback collection.

options.name: Aggregate-only monitoring
options.description: Reliance on aggregate entropy, reward, or global KL metrics without tool-conditioned or slice-level signals.

options.name: Reference-support distribution monitoring
options.description: Monitoring reference-policy probability support and state-distribution mixtures in tool-conditioned regions.

options.name: Importance-weight monitoring
options.description: Monitoring importance weights, support, and denominator sensitivity, especially in tail or low-support regions.

options.name: Shadow decision execution
options.description: Execute candidate decisions without applying them to production outcomes before promotion.

options.name: Unpressured monitoring
options.description: Monitors behavior without applying optimization pressure to the monitoring setup.

options.name: Reward-hacking trip-wire monitoring
options.description: Introduces deliberate vulnerabilities with monitoring and alerts to detect reward hacking.

options.name: Shadow-run metrics collection
options.description: Collects live-like metrics during shadow execution to bridge offline evaluation and deployment.

options.name: Parallel shadow logging
options.description: Logs decisions and context in parallel while a candidate policy executes in shadow mode.

options.name: Interaction audit logging
options.description: Retains interaction records and explanations for operational, regulatory, and post-deployment oversight.

options.name: Reference-data coverage monitoring
options.description: Monitors whether incoming requests are covered by the external reference data used at serving time.

options.name: Reward-hack behavior documentation
options.description: Documents exploit behavior and circumstances for production analysis and remediation.

options.name: Automated evaluation metrics
options.description: Uses fast automated quality metrics to monitor adaptation and deployed behavior.

options.name: Evaluator position-consistency monitoring
options.description: Monitoring evaluator judgments after swapping response positions to detect positional inconsistency and bias.

options.name: Scratchpad-based reasoning observability
options.description: Expose intermediate reasoning traces to inspect hidden behavior associated with reward hacking.

options.name: Hint-based faithfulness evaluation
options.description: Provide correct and incorrect hints and test whether reported reasoning acknowledges influential information.

options.name: Light reasoning-trace optimization
options.description: Applying limited optimization pressure to reasoning traces without directly strongly supervising their content.

options.name: Direct strong chain-of-thought supervision
options.description: Strongly supervising chain-of-thought outputs as a training signal.

options.name: Penalized undesirable thoughts
options.description: Penalizing undesirable reasoning content as an intervention to prevent monitored misbehavior.

options.name: Multi-objective evaluation suite
options.description: Use complementary metrics so an agent cannot optimize one metric while degrading related objectives.

options.name: Held-out environment testing
options.description: Evaluate agents in environments different from training conditions to reveal environment-specific shortcuts.

options.name: Human review of high-stakes behavior
options.description: Retain human review for unusually behaving or apparently high-performing agents in consequential applications.

options.name: Open-source post-training diagnostics
options.description: Using released detection, evaluation, and annotation infrastructure for reproducible post-training monitoring.

options.name: Manual human monitoring at scale
options.description: Relying on manual review of agent actions as the primary deployed behavioral monitoring approach.

options.name: Adversarial-policy evaluation
options.description: A deployed or victim policy is tested against strategically trained adversarial policies.

options.name: Human feedback loop
options.description: Collect post-deployment human feedback and feed it into model or policy updates.

options.name: Chain-of-Thought sole-safeguard reliance
options.description: Treating Chain-of-Thought monitoring as sufficient to rule out deceptive or undesirable behavior.

options.name: Process-level supervision
options.description: Supervises intermediate reasoning or behavior steps rather than judging only final outputs.

options.name: Outcome-only reward evaluation
options.description: Evaluates only final outputs without intermediate-step supervision.

options.name: Programmatic intermediate verification
options.description: Uses objective tests to verify intermediate generated behavior where reliable verification is available.

options.name: Internal principle checklists
options.description: Uses structured internal checkpoints to evaluate reasoning beyond a single scalar outcome.

options.name: Reasoning propensity measurement
options.description: Measures the tendency to produce particular kinds of reasoning to assess monitoring effectiveness.

options.name: Domain-specific evaluation benchmarks
options.description: Evaluates deployed behavior against industry-specific accuracy, coding, recognition, or compliance requirements.

options.name: LLM-as-a-judge evaluation
options.description: Uses a stronger model for pairwise comparison and reasoning-quality or compliance assessment.

options.name: Threshold-triggered monitoring response
options.description: Initiates operational response when a monitored production-quality or service metric crosses a configured threshold, without requiring rollout callbacks or persistence checks.

options.name: Rollout-callback diagnostic response
options.description: Initiates degradation diagnostics from rollout lifecycle callbacks, typically using threshold checks at those rollout points rather than evaluating every environment step.

options.name: Multi-signal SLO-governed rollback response
options.description: Initiates or controls rollback through a coordinated policy combining threshold checks, rollout diagnostics, persistence requirements, calibrated trigger levels, and SLO-aware serving protections.

options.name: Weighted reward-mean test
options.description: Compare sequential rewards using a covariance-aware weighted mean rather than an unweighted recent mean.

options.name: Inverse-covariance row-sum weighting
options.description: Derive reward weights from row sums of the inverse covariance matrix under a normal-reward assumption.

options.name: Naive simple-mean benchmark
options.description: Use the simple mean as a conventional comparison detector in RL monitoring experiments.

options.name: Complete-episode bootstrap statistic
options.description: Bootstrapping complete episodes to preserve dependence structure when constructing degradation thresholds.

options.name: BFAR-based drift detection test
options.description: Use BFAR as the primary test for detecting deployed-agent degradation.

options.name: Recent-episode simple-mean detector
options.description: Compare the recent reward mean with a reference mean; explicitly characterized as suboptimal for degradation detection.

options.name: CUSUM detector benchmark
options.description: Use CUSUM as a competing sequential-testing method for detecting reward degradation.

options.name: Hotelling mean-shift benchmark
options.description: Use Hotelling’s multivariate mean-shift test as a competing degradation detector.

options.name: Moving-average reward detector
options.description: Detecting degradation from a configurable moving average of recent episode rewards.

options.name: Multi-metric reward monitoring
options.description: Monitors several complementary reward or performance metrics to detect divergence and degradation.

options.name: Cross-metric degradation detection
options.description: Detects improvement in an optimized metric accompanied by deterioration in complementary metrics.

options.name: Original-data mixing
options.description: Mix original training data with new fine-tuning data to preserve prior capabilities.

options.name: Rehearsal cache
options.description: Retain important historical samples for rehearsal during continual fine-tuning.

options.name: Continual dataset refresh
options.description: Refresh policy-training data continually to reduce staleness in changing environments.

options.name: Preference propagation across datasets
options.description: Amplifying limited human preference data across larger training or monitoring datasets.

options.name: Counterfactual testing in CI/CD
options.description: Test alternative policy actions offline before deployment without unsafe online exploration.

options.name: Policy safety gates
options.description: Require offline evaluation and simulated safety checks before staging or production promotion.

options.name: Shadow deployment
options.description: Observe a candidate policy under production conditions without allowing it to affect live decisions.

options.name: Canary or blue-green rollout
options.description: Limit production exposure through controlled rollout patterns that support observation and containment.

options.name: Counterfactual policy-value gating
options.description: Uses logged-data estimates and their uncertainty to gate policy promotion.

options.name: Automated policy rollback
options.description: Automatically restore a known-good policy when regressions or safety-SLO violations occur.

options.name: State restoration for stateful policies
options.description: Restore or reset online-learning state in addition to replacing the policy version.

options.name: Automated circuit breakers
options.description: Automatic protective intervention detects degraded performance and switches or contains the deployed policy.

options.name: Safe fallback policies
options.description: A degraded agent is switched to a predefined safer policy during recovery.

options.name: Incident-capable on-call recovery
options.description: Assigning authorized on-call personnel to disable unsafe policies and activate fallback behavior.

options.name: Runbook-based incident recovery
options.description: Using stepwise runbooks for known incidents and coordinated playbooks for complex policy failures.

options.name: Fail-safe degradation handling
options.description: Keep deployed agents operating safely or recover gracefully when learning or environmental conditions cause poor performance.

options.name: Offline RL for constrained environments
options.description: Use offline RL when online interaction is dangerous, costly, or legally restricted.

options.name: Online or hybrid experimentation
options.description: Use online or hybrid methods when safe experimentation is possible but logged data is limited.

options.name: Nonrepresentative-log offline RL
options.description: Use offline RL despite nonrepresentative logs or poorly defined rewards; explicitly rejected as unreliable.

options.name: Batch-constrained deep Q-learning
options.description: Offline learning constrains value updates to the support of a fixed dataset to limit extrapolation risk.

options.name: Conservative Q-learning
options.description: Offline value estimation is deliberately conservative to reduce overoptimistic production policies.

options.name: Pairwise LLM feedback scoring
options.description: Using pairwise LLM judgments converted through Bradley–Terry scoring to guide feedback optimization.

options.name: Ray-based RL framework
options.description: Using Ray as the framework for rapidly starting and scaling reinforcement-learning workloads.

options.name: Amazon SageMaker RL platform
options.description: Using managed Amazon SageMaker RL services to move reinforcement-learning development into production-scale workloads.

options.name: Conservative offline objective
options.description: Using conservative objectives and regularization to limit offline overfitting and risky policy behavior.

options.name: Scheduled fine-tuning jobs
options.description: Collect recent data and perform evaluated nightly or weekly incremental updates.

options.name: Continuous online model updating
options.description: Update deployed models from new information and feedback in near real time.

options.name: Metric-triggered retraining
options.description: Starting retraining when monitored performance crosses a threshold instead of only following a calendar.

options.name: Automated drift-to-deployment retraining
options.description: Automating monitoring, drift detection, retraining, validation, and deployment as one adaptation workflow.

options.name: Selective component retraining
options.description: Updating selected model components rather than all weights to reduce adaptation effort.

options.name: Rolling PEFT fine-tuning
options.description: Use parameter-efficient rolling updates to keep deployed models fresh without full retraining.

options.name: Micro-batch or single-sample updates
options.description: Apply updates at streaming micro-batch or individual-sample granularity.

options.name: Immediate feedback incorporation
options.description: Fine-tune immediately after a user rejects or corrects a deployed-system response.

options.name: Human-escalated corrective update
options.description: Escalate detected production problems to human review or retraining before or alongside automated updating.

options.name: Engagement-driven self-refinement
options.description: Refining deployed outputs or policy using engagement feedback.

options.name: API-error-driven policy refinement
options.description: Adapting policy behavior after tool or API errors to recover from deployment failures.

options.name: Retrieval and model-editing adaptation
options.description: Updates deployed models through retrieval augmentation or targeted editing instead of full retraining.

options.name: Supervised fine-tuning
options.description: Updates a pretrained model by imitating curated demonstrations before or during alignment operations.

options.name: Production policy freezing
options.description: Freezing deployed policies and allowing updates only after offline or controlled testing.

options.name: Human-escalated policy correction
options.description: Using human review and supervision to steer or adjust deployed policy behavior after observed issues.

options.name: MLOps-integrated refresh workflow
options.description: Integrating deployment monitoring, feedback collection, and recurring model refreshes into repeatable operational pipelines.

options.name: Distributed-aware metric monitoring
options.description: Metrics account for cross-rank aggregation, stragglers, and memory imbalance during distributed training.

options.name: Serving-time computation reuse
options.description: Reuse serving-generated intermediate computations during training to reduce repeated forward-pass work.

options.name: Fixed-base continuously learned adapter
options.description: Update a LoRA adapter continuously while keeping the base model fixed.

options.name: Reversible adapter updates
options.description: Swap in new adapters and revert them when operational or behavioral problems occur.

options.name: GPU-backed inference serving
options.description: Use accelerator-backed serving to meet deployed model latency and throughput requirements.

options.name: Quantized or distilled model serving
options.description: Reduce serving resource requirements through quantization or knowledge distillation while preserving alignment.

options.name: Request batching
options.description: Batch inference requests to improve aggregate serving throughput.

options.name: Constrained or conservative policy updates
options.description: Limit policy changes or enforce safety constraints during learning to reduce catastrophic degradation.

options.name: Policy-managed warm pool
options.description: Serving infrastructure maintains a warm pool whose pre-warming behavior is controlled by a learned policy.

options.name: Temporal and user-context serving features
options.description: Supplying temporal patterns and user context as policy inputs for serving-time prediction.

options.name: Multi-model endpoint serving
options.description: Consolidating multiple policy models behind one serving endpoint.

options.name: Training-serving process co-location
options.description: Place training and serving processes together to support faster online updates.

options.name: Rapid serving-to-training data transfer
options.description: Feed serving data quickly to a separate training cluster rather than updating serving servers directly.

options.name: On-device edge inference placement
options.description: Running the deployed policy directly on edge devices under device compute and storage constraints.

options.name: CloudWatch print-log storage
options.description: Centralize operational training print logs in CloudWatch.

options.name: S3 training-output storage
options.description: Persist training outputs, metrics, and artifacts in durable object storage.

options.name: Experiment configuration tracking
options.description: Track state representations, reward functions, algorithms, hyperparameters, and job variations.

options.name: Single-click training-job replication
options.description: Replicate training jobs easily to support reproducibility and investigation.

options.name: Registry-anchored policy lineage
options.description: Tracks deployed policy versions through their training histories and uses model-registry status to identify rollback targets. This provides basic traceability for deployment and recovery.

options.name: Auditable rollback lineage
options.description: Combines registry-based rollback targeting with explicit audit records of rollback triggers, source versions, target versions, and timing.

options.name: End-to-end deployment evidence lineage
options.description: Links live endpoints and variants to training jobs and retained inference data, while anchoring deployed versions and rollback targets in policy lineage records.

options.name: Operational capture with environment isolation
options.description: Retains production inference records while separating training infrastructure from serving infrastructure to protect production stability and latency.

options.name: Runtime action shield
options.description: An architectural layer intercepts policy actions between the agent and environment and blocks or replaces unsafe actions.

options.name: Static dynamics-based shielding
options.description: Shield decisions rely on fixed transition-dynamics, hidden-parameter, and hazard-boundary assumptions.

options.name: Shield-only safety architecture
options.description: Treating the runtime shield as the complete safety mechanism without measuring interventions under changed conditions.

options.name: Unsafe-action blocking or replacement
options.description: Blocking unsafe policy actions or substituting safer actions before environment execution.

options.name: Adaptive action shielding
options.description: Runtime shielding adapts its safe-action gate to detected distribution shifts or uncertainty.

options.name: Adaptive hidden-parameter shielding
options.description: Infer changing hidden risk parameters online and shield unsafe policy actions.

options.name: Deployment-time action constraints
options.description: Enforces allowed-action limits at deployment before policy actions reach the environment.

options.name: Business-rule validation
options.description: Validates generated or extracted outputs against structured operational and compliance rules.

options.name: Prompt-injection output guardrail
options.description: Runtime filtering or blocking that prevents prompt-injection attempts from producing unsafe agent outputs.

options.name: Restricted-topic output enforcement
options.description: Runtime enforcement that blocks responses on sensitive or prohibited topics.

options.name: Ethical monitoring framework
options.description: Guides production monitoring and model governance through explicit ethical principles addressing bias and unsafe behavior.

options.name: Explainable monitoring decisions
options.description: Provides mechanisms that make model decisions and monitoring judgments understandable and auditable to stakeholders.

options.name: Transparent decision-making
options.description: Requires stakeholders to understand decision rationale rather than treating monitoring and model behavior as a black box.

options.name: Regulatory accountability controls
options.description: Uses formal accountability and fairness controls to satisfy evolving AI governance and compliance expectations.

options.name: Black-box decision-making
options.description: Leaves production decisions opaque to stakeholders and auditors.

options.name: Ongoing bias monitoring
options.description: Continuously checks deployed decisions for bias introduced by feedback, annotation, or model behavior.

options.name: Cross-functional monitoring governance
options.description: Joint interpretation of technical drift, domain changes, and business impact by ML, operations, and domain stakeholders.

options.name: Business-impact monitoring integration
options.description: Linking monitoring to analytics and reporting dashboards for business, safety, accuracy, and satisfaction outcomes.
